Area of Effect (AoE) abilities impact multiple targets within a specific area. These abilities can deal damage, heal, or apply effects to all targets within a radius, making them essential for managing groups of enemies or supporting allies. AoE spells can be ground-targeted, centered on the caster, or focused on a location.

Dispels remove harmful or beneficial effects from a target. They cleanse debuffs like poisons, diseases, curses, and magic effects from allies or remove buffs from enemies. Dispels counter crowd control, negate damaging debuffs, and weaken opponents.
Adopt a specialized Stance, Transformation, or Shapeshift effect that grants access to specific powerful abilities while limiting others. Only one Form can be activated at a time.
Buffs are positive passive effects for you and your allies.

Core base attacks. All of these abilities are spammable without a cooldown.

Crowd control is tactical skills designed to manipulate and temporarily impair enemies by stunning them, immobilizing them in place, silencing their spellcasting, or even transforming them into harmless creatures.

Damage Over Time (DoT) abilities deal damage to a target gradually over a set period rather than delivering a single burst of damage. These abilities continuously apply their effects, ticking at regular intervals, and can be useful for sustaining damage on enemies while the caster focuses on other actions.

Debuffs are curses, charms, roars, magical effects and more that can be put on enemies. These can make them weaker, slower, or hurt them over time. There are different types of debuffs like poison, disease, curse, and magic, each needing specific ways to remove them.

Healing spells are core abilities that restore health to allies. They are essential for keeping a group alive in combat. These spells counter damage, sustain allies, and ensure survivability during battles.

Masteries allow you to learn entire categories of spells without using any more gem slots and using less Ability Essence. For Example, with Seal Mastery you can learn every Seal for less Ability Essence and Gems.

Combat Healers seamlessly weave back and forth between healing allies and damaging enemies: oftentimes doing both simultaneously. Many Combat Healers heal by siphoning life from foes and giving it to their allies. Others build up power by healing to unleash devastating spells on enemies. While not as potent as their Pure Healer counterparts, Combat Healers make up for it by assisting in dealing damage and slaying enemies faster.

Hybrid heroes have mastered the art of martial and magical combat, becoming spellswords. They seamlessly blend their mage-craft into dazzling displays of close-range fighting, infusing elemental might into their weapons, cleaving through foes with frozen blades, or even using shadow magic to enhance their assassination abilities. Some Hybrid augment their fighting capabilities with a single element, while others use powerful manipulative and control spells to become better warriors.

Magic heroes weave the mystical arts into all manner of destructive and defensive spells. They excel at dealing damage to both single targets and large groups, raining fire, frost, arcane, nature, shadow, or holy damage upon their foes. While most Magic heroes prefer to remain at a distance, many have found ways to channel their spellcraft into powerful defensive spells, using their Mana as a means to defend against harm. Whether acting as a Wizard or an indomitable Mage Knight, Magic heroes are forces of destruction on the battlefield.

Melee heroes are masters of close-quarters combat, relying on their weapons to unleash savage attacks. From knights and rogues to lancers, barbarians, and monks, they weave through enemies and strike with unmatched force and precision. Melee fighters excel at delivering raw, powerful blows and can sometimes cleave through multiple foes at once. Always on the front lines, these warriors embody the essence of ferocity and skill, turning the tide of battle with relentless attacks and unwavering resolve.

Pure Healers focus entirely on restoring and rejuvenating allies. Able to not only heal and resurrect, but also shield and prevent damage entirely, Pure Healers devote their attention and mana more to their party than to enemies. Using powerful direct heals, buffs, and control spells, they keep their party strong and moving forward.

Ranged heroes are agile, deadly warriors that excel at slaying enemies from a distance. Precise and accurate, they remain out of harms way so they can focus entirely on the offense. Ranged heroes deliver deliver swift, lethal shots and stings from long-range, peppering enemies with arrows and bullets. Rangers, archers, and gunmen all fall within this category.

Barbaric fighters, agile assassins, and powerful wizards all share a common goal: swiftly disposing of their enemies. Whether through a mighty storm of steel or a torrent or arcane magic, those who focus on slaying foes are known as Damage Dealers (DPS). This role encompasses the widest variety of Heroes: from wandering knights to rangers, thieves, and sorcerers. To walk this path is to embrace destruction.
Healers are powerful spellcasters that wield their magic to bolster and rejuvenate allies. Able to buff, restore, and even resurrect fallen friends, most Healers are students of either the Holy Light or the eternal cycle of Nature. Some healers even weave these elements into more offensive schools, wielding holy cauterizing fire or soothing allies with frozen heals. With large pools of magic and an array of supportive spells, they are the backbone of their party, ensuring everyone can charge forward into danger.
Tanks are indomitable bulwarks that absorb and deflect damage, taking hits so that the rest of the party stays safe. They are the vanguard of any group, using shields, heavy armor, monstrous transform effects, and sometimes even raw agility to block, dodge, parry, and shrug off incoming effects. With high health and defensive abilities, Tanks hold foes’ attention while the rest of the party does their job.

A radiant vessel of Holy power that marks allies with Holy light. As a Hierophant, you'll energize party members with your Renew spell before channeling direct heals. These direct heals radiate to all other party members graced by your Renew, causing wave after wave of holy healing.

Agile and charismatic, Swashbucklers are pirates, mercenaries, and rogues who are so skilled with a single off-hand weapon that they can effortlessly deflect and parry incoming blows. Their free hand allows them to use unique abilities and flourishes, delivering quick strikes and ripostes to counter the enemy's attacks.

An eerie blend of mysticism and malevolence, Vampire Lords wield shadowy magic that leeches life from foes and transfers it to allies. Wrapped in shadows and wielding unholy light, the more damage you inflict on foes, the more your allies benefit. Siphon life to restore your party in a sanguine display of cursed magic.

Attacking from above your target offers a significant advantage, and no one excels at this more than a Paratrooper. As a Paratrooper, you'll launch yourself high into the air, gaining bonus damage when firing on enemies below you. A combat parachute slows your descent, not only improving your accuracy but also increasing the time you spend out of harm's way.

Become an unstoppable force and charge through foes as a Heavyweight, a colossal fighter wielding a massive two-handed weapon. As a Heavyweight, you build up momentum by using various physical abilities before unleashing it all in a single devastating strike. A juggernaut of raw destruction, Heavyweights smash through enemies with earth-shattering blows that leave the ground trembling in their wake.

Bold and dedicated clerics, Eternal Caretakers stand beside their allies in the heat of combat. Staunch and unflinching, their powerful Halo skill emits a wave of healing energy that sweeps out over nearby allies. Casting other healing spells reduces Halo's cooldown.

Capture the magic of the Bronze Dragonflight and wield it as your own. As a Steward of Eternity, you'll rewind time for your allies and prevent wounds before they even occur. Place timed heals on allies that restore health after a moment, and use Arcane magic to synchronize party members' health.

Cryotherapists weave brilliant light into glistening crystals, becoming clerics of frost. As a Cryotherapist, you'll use Frostbolts to charge up Holy energy before unleashing cool winds to soothe allies' wounds. A crippling threat to foes and a chill boon to allies, Cryotherapists find a home in any party.

Embrace the Shadow and become a Dark Ranger, wielding the power of the Banshee Queen as your own. As a Dark Ranger, you infuse your shots with Shadow damage, peppering foes in a flurry of sinister arrows. As you grow in strength, you'll gain the ability to weave Shadow Bolts into your arrows, dealing massive damage with each shot.

Grove Keepers are masters of nature, utilizing healing spells that rejuvenate multiple party members at once. These powerful spells overflow from one ally to the next, ensuring that your entire group can stay in the fight.

Legends once spoke of Hunters who soul-bonded with their animal companions, becoming a single unit of bestial wrath. Able to channel their beast's inner rage, these Bestial Rangers lurk on the fringes of society, serving as savage mercenaries or stoic guides. As a Bestial Ranger, you share your companion's thirst for blood and can enrage alongside them to tear foes to shreds.

Locust Rangers are hunters who have learned to weave natural magics into their shots and stings. Able to poison enemies from a distance, they can weave Druidic magic into their arrows and fire off instant spells. From infusing arrows with wrath to sending out swarms of locusts onto foes, Locust Rangers specialize in quick, consistent damage. Their strongest arrows cause a buildup of poison on targets which can burst for bonus Nature damage.

Mend your allies in the light of dawn. As a Dawnkeeper, you'll designate one party member to serve as a Beacon of Light. When you heal your Beacon with Holy Light, the power swells and bursts, healing nearby allies. Support your Beacon and light the way through the darkness!

Once trained to hunt the demons of the Burning Legion, Wardens surge through the battlefield in a flash of steel. As a Warden, your arsenal of weapons makes you deadly both up-close and from afar. Carve through enemies with a massive two-handed spear, then effortlessly finish fleeing foes with your glaive.

Overcome by the deadly diseases of the Tainted Grove, these Druids of Rot transform into monstrous bears plagued with disease. Every swipe of their tainted claws corrupts foes, causing Infected Blood, which deals damage-over-time.

Powerful Mages devote themselves to the study of Frost, Fire, or Arcane magic; rarely do any attempt mastery of all three. You are no ordinary Mage. As an Evoker, you effortlessly weave all three elements into an unstoppable onslaught. Your Frostbolt spell triggers instant Fireballs and Arcane Missiles, allowing you to combine your magic in a devastating display of power. Damage foes with bursts of different elemental blasts and bring them to their knees.

Some tanks believe their shield is a tool for defense, but you know better: as a Relentless, you use your shield as an offensive weapon of devastating power. Your strikes reduce the cooldown of your Shield Slam ability, allowing you to incorporate it into your onslaught. Build up Combo Points and unleash powerful combo strikes.

Surrender to the whispers of the Void and become a Shadow Druid. Nightmare Beasts are corrupted Dire Bears who trade physical damage for savage, Shadow claws. As an emissary of the Emerald Nightmare, your twisted claws spread Corruption to enemies. Powerful Nightmare Beasts can even launch devastating Shadow Bolts while in their monstrous Dire Bear form.

The Night Elves of Teldrassil are no strangers to the power of the Moon; its energy fuels their strongest warriors and illuminates their people in the darkness. You, however, revere the Moon in a more profound way. As a Druid of the Eclipse, you channel power from both the Sun and the Moon. During your Lunar Phase, unleash crippling magic that deals damage over time. During your Solar Phase, switch to devastating single-target damage.

The most skilled archers on Azeroth are known as Marksmen: precise, accurate, and deadly snipers. Whether wielding a bow or a gun, these hunters possess the grace and techniques of trained rogues, executing complex trick shots and striking multiple targets at once.

Transform into a beast of raw carnage and blood. As a Carnage Incarnate, you empower your bear form with bloody strikes that rend your foes, draining them of life. Your attacks deal crippling damage to multiple enemies at once, leaving a trail of destruction in your wake.

Unleash the fury of thunder and lightning! As a Storm Giant, you are a hulking avatar of the storm's fury. Blast enemies with thunder and lightning to electrocute multiple foes at once, and use massive weapons to charge your unrelenting maelstrom. Your hits charge up your legendary Lightning Blade, which instantly strikes foes for massive Nature damage.

Warlocks who succumb to rampant Fel magic become Demoniacs: corrupted demons of the Twisting Nether. As a Demoniac, you trade your mortal coil for enhanced health and defense, as well as unique Demon abilities. Burn foes surrounding you with a blazing Immolation Aura, and cleave enemies for Shadow damage with Demonic claws.

Wielding the power of the Holy Light, Crusaders are the embodiments of divine justice. Often likened to angelic warriors, Crusaders Consecrate both their weapons and the ground beneath them, igniting foes in righteous fire. As a Crusader, your Seal spells boast considerable strength, allowing your weapon to deal bonus damage. Your divine fury is relentless, your justice law. Use your array of Holy weapons to bathe the wicked in Holy flames, leaving only the righteous standing.

Wreathed in an icy cloak of Frost, the Icebound are cold, dark wraiths bound to the frozen wastes of Northrend. Though physically frail, Icebound are masters of turning Frost into magical bulwarks. As an Icebound, your spells reduce the cooldown of your Ice Barrier, granting you rapid and nearly impenetrable defense.

A Recipe teaches your character how to craft a specific item within a Profession. 

Recipes can be learned from a Profession Trainer, purchased from Vendors, traded between players, or looted from enemies throughout the world.
A mount is a player-controlled ride used to travel faster across the world—but only outdoors.

An arena is a fast-paced, instanced PvP battle to the death. Players can fight in 1v1, 2v2, or 3v3 styled teams to test their skills in a casual or competitive clash! 

You can queue for an Arena with the PvP menu (Hotkey H -> Choose Skirmish for a casual arena, or find the Rated tab for a competitive experience)!

Ascension’s seasonal realms are time-limited servers that reset at the end of each season. 

They often feature unique game modes and progression that begins in Vanilla content and advances through to the current patch on Area: 52.

Bloodforged equipment is Soulbound PvE gear that has been transformed into Bind-on-Equip PvP gear.

To Bloodforge an item, it must first be Soulbound, then combined with a Bloody Jar which is available to purchase from Nozdormu.

Character Info (Hotkey C) displays your equipped gear and current stats. Hover over any stat or item for detailed information. From this menu, you can save equipment sets, assign a cosmetic title to your character, and review character currencies.
Crafting Professions use materials gathered from the world, or looted from enemies, to create equipment, enhancements, and consumables.

Dungeons are five-player instanced challenges featuring elite mobs, tough bosses, and valuable loot. 

You can either find their entrances in the open world or use the Dungeon Finder to join a group instantly.

First aid is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession that lets you craft bandages, which restore health over time and can be used during combat.

First aid uses cloth dropped from humanoid enemies for materials.
Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that boosts your attack speed, casting speed, and energy regeneration, letting you unleash abilities more rapidly.

Jewelcrafting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that creates jewelry, trinkets, and gems to enhance your equipment.

Jewelcrafting is reliant on Mining for materials.
Millhouse Manastorm is a quirky and well-loved gnome who guides you through the Manastorm and trades Bedlam Bullions for a variety of cosmetic and convenience items.

Mythic+ dungeons are timed, repeatable challenges that scale in difficulty based on your mythic keystone level, adding affixes that change weekly to keep gameplay dynamic. 

Completing runs quickly upgrades your key and boosts rewards, offering some of the best gear and progression in PvE content.

Primary Attributes (also known as Primary Stats) define your character’s power and shape their combat style. 

Choose one in the Character Advancement menu (Hotkey N) to perfect your hero and develop your chosen playstyle.

Quest Givers are NPCs who offer quests to players. 

These NPCs are marked with icons above their heads that indicate the status of a quest and upon completion, can give items, Experience, and Reputation as rewards.
Silas Darkmoon is a key Wildcard NPC who grants Scrolls of Fortune while leveling, offers max-level Scrolls for Marks of Ascension, sells Skill Card Packs, and accepts Darkmoon Tickets for rewards.

Stamina is a Primary Attribute available to all players. 

It represents your character’s overall toughness and endurance, directly increasing your total health pool.

Talents are powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock new tools, helping define your character’s combat style. 

Each class has three possible talent trees, and the more Talent Essences you invest in each tree, the more powerful talents you can obtain.
The Book of Artisans is a Profession Trainer in the form of a summonable Companion that can teach your character any Profession or Recipe that’s available from other Profession Trainers.

The Guild Bank is a large shared storage accessible at major cities where guild members can store and share items or gold. 

Guild leaders control permissions and can purchase additional tabs for gold as the Guild grows.
The Skills tab (Hotkey K) provides a detailed overview of your character’s various proficiencies like weapon skills, Profession level, and languages.

This is a ruleset that allows players to engage in open-world PvP and loot gear and items from defeated opponents but risk losing their own if they die. 

Equipment can be protected using Fel Commutation for a price, and looted items become powerful Bloodforged gear.

Using a Feather of the Ancients instantly unlocks all Flightpaths for your character. 

Feathers are stored in your Vanity Collection and can be obtained from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency, as well as the Ascension Store for Donation Points.

Your Mystic Enchant Collection (N -> Mystic Enchant -> Enchant Collection) stores enchants saved with Mystic Extracts. 

This menu is shared across all characters on the same realm, and is accessible at any Enchanting Altar to apply enchants to your active slots.

A Mystic Scroll is an item that contains a powerful Mystic Enchant, which can enhance your character’s abilities and playstyle. These scrolls serve as the primary way to obtain new enchants and experiment with different build options.

You can apply a mystic scroll directly to one of your Active Enchant Slots at any time without needing an Enchanting Altar. Doing so immediately grants the enchant’s benefits but consumes the scroll, so it’s a one-time use unless you acquire another copy.

If you want to keep the enchant permanently for future use, you can take the scroll to an Enchanting Altar and use a Mystic Extract to save the enchant into your Mystic Enchant Collection. This allows you to apply the saved enchant repeatedly without using up more scrolls.

Alternatively, you can reforge your mystic scroll at an Enchanting Altar using Marks of Ascension to transform the scroll into a different, randomly selected enchant. This system system lets you learn undiscovered enchants or try new effects without needing to find or buy new scrolls.

A mount is a player-controlled creature that boosts movement speed for faster travel. Found in the Pets Tab (Hotkey Shift + P), mounts are vital for leveling, exploration, and convenience, and come in various cosmetic styles and types. The various mount types provide unique advantages based on the terrain.

Ground Mounts:
Unlocked first, these mounts increase movement speed by 40%, with higher speeds available from Riding Trainers. Usable only outdoors, they dismount you in buildings, or when using certain abilities. All mounts can function as ground mounts, regardless of type.

Flying Mounts:
These mounts enable aerial travel in zones that support it (Outland and Northrend). Flying mounts require flight training and the proper zone; otherwise, they act as ground mounts.

Aquatic Mounts:
Designed for swimming, these mounts boost swim speed but offer little to no speed on land. Ideal for underwater activities, these rare mounts offer unique utility.

Mounts can be obtained through quests, achievements, Vendors, the Auction House, seasonal events, or purchased from the Ascension Store.

Ameer Greatluck is a helpful NPC located in all Capital Cities who provides access to the Recovery Services menu which can restore accidentally lost items. You can reach this service by clicking the (?) icon in your Micro Menu or by speaking directly to Ameer.

Through Recovery Services, you can reclaim items that were sold to a Vendor, deleted, or even disenchanted. Whether it’s a rare drop or a piece of important gear, Ameer Greatluck gives you a second chance to recover your lost valuables.

Armor is a defensive stat that reduces the physical damage your character receives. It is found on most pieces of gear, and its value is heavily influenced by the item’s Armor Type (such as cloth, leather, mail, or plate).

The higher your armor rating, the less damage you take from physical attacks, making it a key stat for survivability in both PvE and PvP.

You can view your current Armor value in Character Info (Hotkey C).

Bedlam bullions are a Realm-Bound Currency earned by completing Manastorm levels for the first time. Each new level cleared rewards you with a set amount of bullions, and higher levels grant more, encouraging steady progression through the endless dungeon. However, re-clearing previously completed levels does not award additional bullions, only your first clear of each floor counts.

You can view your current amount of bedlam bullions in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab). Because they’re Realm-Bound, bullions can’t be traded or sold to other players, but they’re shared across all of your characters on the same realm.

You can spend your bedlam bullions at Millhouse Manastorm for cosmetic equipment, convenience items, novelty toys, Tamed Pet appearances, and Companions.

Cogsworth is an NPC vendor located near Millhouse Manastorm at the entrance of your Capital City. He plays an important role in the Manastorm system, offering a variety of Manastorm Spells and upgrade items in exchange for Bonzo Bolts which is a Currency earned by progressing through the Manastorm.

The items Cogsworth sells are designed to enhance your effectiveness in the Manastorm, from powerful spells that help in tougher encounters to useful upgrades that provide more control, survivability, or utility as you climb.

Currency refers to various special tokens and points used to purchase items, services, and unique rewards. These points are not stored in your inventory and cannot be traded or bought on the Auction House. 

You can view all your currencies in the currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

Examples of currency are:

Honor Points
Arena Points
Marks of Ascension
Seasonal Points
Tokens of Prestige

Enchanting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that enhances weapons and armor with magical effects to improve combat performance.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn enchanting. Once you've trained the skill, you can start collecting materials by disenchanting equipment of uncommon, rare, or epic quality. This process destroys the item, converting it into materials like dusts, essences, and shards, which are used to create enchantments. 

As you progress, you'll unlock Recipes, called formulas, that let you apply specific enchantments to gear.

Enchanting your own gear only uses materials, but selling or storing enchantments requires Enchanting Vellum from Vendors. To avoid vellum costs, use the Trade window to enchant other players’ gear, including Soulbound items.

To perform enchantments, you’ll need to craft a rod. Higher-level enchantments require more advanced rods, so it’s important to upgrade your skill tools as you progress. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

Flightpaths (FP) are a fast-travel system, allowing players to quickly fly between specific, connected locations across the open world. They’re essential for cutting down travel time, especially when questing or moving between distant zones.

To use a flightpath, you must first unlock its node by speaking to the local Flightmaster. You can also instantly unlock certain nodes by using special items like the Feather of the Ancients, which reveals multiple locations at once.

However, you can only fly between nodes that are directly connected and already discovered. If you're trying to travel across multiple zones, you’ll need to have unlocked all the Flightmasters along the route, otherwise, the system won’t allow you to fly to your intended destination.

Once enough nodes are unlocked, you can chain multiple points together to create efficient travel routes, making it much easier to return to old quest hubs, dungeons, or cities.

Flightpaths are accessed through any Flightmaster, typically marked with a wing icon on your World Map and mini-map. When planning your journey, be sure to use the Map Lens to find nearby Flightmasters and keep your travel network growing.

Heirlooms are special pieces of Realm-Bound gear designed to scale with your character as they level, making them ideal for leveling alternative characters or speeding up the journey to maximum level. These items not only increase in power as your character gains levels, but many also provide bonus Experience, helping you level faster through quests, kills, and battlegrounds.

Heirlooms are stored in your Vanity Collection and are accessible to all characters on the same realm. Once unlocked, you can equip heirlooms on any eligible character, giving you a powerful head start with solid stats and consistent performance across all level ranges.

Most heirlooms come in the form of weapons, armor, and trinkets, and some are themed to match specific class roles, such as Strength-based melee, Intellect-based casters, or Agility-based archers.

Heirlooms can be obtained through various means, including purchasing them from Vendors for PvP Points, Prestige Points, Marks of Ascension, and from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

Intellect is the Primary Attribute that represents mental acuity, magical knowledge, and the ability to harness arcane, divine, or elemental forces. It is a core stat for players who specialize in spellcasting, making it vital for dealing magic damage, healing allies, or using utility spells effectively.

Effects of intellect:

+1 Intellect increases your maximum Mana by 15.
+1 Intellect increases your Spell and Melee Critical Strike Rating.

Intellect also affects Mana Regeneration indirectly, especially when paired with Spirit or talents that scale from intellect.

Marks of Ascension are a versatile Currency earned from virtually every type of content in the game including quests, Dungeons, PvP, Raids, and world events. These tokens are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and serve as one of the primary ways to progress and refine your character.

Marks of Ascension are used whenever unlearning and reassigning your Talents. Alternatively, they can also be spent at Nozdormu for a wide selection of items. These include full Talent Purges, gear, Heirlooms, and other convenient tools to enhance your power or level up faster.

Mystic Extracts are a Currency used to permanently save Mystic Enchants from Mystic Scrolls into your Mystic Enchant Collection. Once an enchant is extracted and added to your collection, you can freely apply it to your character’s Active Enchant Slots using Mystic Orbs, without needing to rely on scrolls or reforging again. You can view your Mystic Extracts in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

You earn 1 mystic extract every time you gain a Mystic Enchanting Level, which happens as you continue to reforge Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar. Each new level reflects your progress and familiarity with the enchantment system and rewards you with another Extract to use.

In addition to leveling up through reforging, you can also gain Mystic Extracts by using a Mystic Draught, an item available from various in-game Vendors. These draughts provide an instant extract and are a great option for players who want to speed up their collection progress or focus on unlocking specific enchants more quickly.

Prestige is a feature that allows you to reset your character back to level 1, wiping all learned abilities and talents while retaining your gear, gold, Mounts, as well as your Reputation standings, Profession levels, and gathered Currency. This system is designed to let you rebuild your character from scratch, offering a fresh leveling experience and the opportunity to experiment with new builds or refine old ones. 

Prestiging offers exclusive rewards like titles, cosmetics, and other unlockables, depending on the realm or seasonal content. 

To Prestige, visit Chromie near the Call Board in your faction’s Capital City.

Raids refer to both a specific type of group as well as a category of high-level PvE content. 

A 'raid group' is a large Party consisting of anywhere from 6 to 40 players, formed when a Party leader converts a standard group using the raid menu (Hotkey O -> Raid Tab -> Convert to Raid). 

Raid groups are typically used for content that requires more coordination and members than regular Dungeons or quests. However, it’s important to note that while in a Raid group, most normal quests won’t track progress.

The term ""raid"" also refers to raid encounters, which are instanced dungeons designed for 10 to 25 players. These encounters feature powerful bosses, complex mechanics, and often require strategic coordination, communication, and strong team builds. Raids offer some of the most prestigious rewards in the game, including high-tier gear, Mounts, cosmetic items, and unique achievements.

Riding Trainers are NPCs found in your Capital City, and occasionally a quest hub, who can teach you how to ride Mounts and improve your riding speed. 

They also provide training for flying Mounts in Outland and Northrend once you reach the appropriate level and requirements. 

Riding comes in several tiers, each increasing your speed and unlocking new movement options:

Apprentice Riding – Increases ground mount speed by 60%.
Journeyman Riding – Upgrades ground mount speed to 100%.
Expert Riding – Unlocks flying at 150% flight speed.
Artisan Riding – Improves flying speed to 280%.
Extraordinary Riding – Grants the maximum flying speed of 310%.

Spell Power (also known as SP) is a secondary stat that increases the damage and healing done by your spells. A higher spell power value means your magical abilities will hit harder or restore more health, making it essential for both casters and hybrid builds.

You can view your spell power in Character Info (Hotkey C).

Strength is the Primary Attribute that represents raw physical power and brute force. It is a key stat for players who want to excel in close-quarters combat, particularly with melee weapons like swords, axes, and maces. Strength increases your Attack Power, which directly boosts the amount of damage your character can deal with physical melee abilities and auto-attacks.

Effects of Strength:

+1 Strength typically increases Melee Attack Power by 2.

Tamed pets are creatures that assist you in battle, each offering unique abilities based on their type. Some pets even come with Pet Talents, allowing you to customize their skills and playstyle to fit your combat needs. You can view the stats and details of your tamed pet in the Pets Tab (Hotkey Shift + P).

You can only have one tamed pet active at a time, but there are many types to choose from, including beasts, demons, undead, dragonkin, and elementals. Summoning a pet depends on its classification and requires specific spells: Tame Beast, Tame Dragonkin, Tether Elemental, Summon Demon, Enslave Demon, and Dominate Undead. 

There are two ways to acquire combat pets: by finding and taming them directly in the open world, or by using a Realm-Bound item known as a pet whistle. Each whistle is tied to a specific pet and can be found in the Wardrobe (Hotkey N -> Wardrobe Tab -> Pets). These whistles can drop from their corresponding creatures in the world, be purchased from the Auction House, or obtained from the Ascension Store using Donation Points (DP).

Pets tamed in the open world must be managed through a stablemaster if you wish to swap between them. However, pets acquired via whistles are far more convenient, allowing you to switch your active pet anytime and anywhere without needing to visit a stable.

The Call Board is a useful quest hub found near the entrances of every Capital City, designed to help players stay on track throughout their journey.

While leveling, the Call Board directs you to the next appropriate questing area, ensuring smooth zone progression and helping you avoid out-leveling content. It’s especially handy for new players or those unsure of where to go next.

At the maximum level, the Call Board offers daily and weekly quests that provide a variety of rewards, including Marks of Ascension, valuable Currency, rare or epic equipment, and more. These quests often encourage players to revisit dungeons, complete world events, or engage in other content that contributes to their overall progression.

For added convenience, you can acquire a portable call board, which lets you access these quests from anywhere in the world. You can buy a call board for your faction or a neutral one that can be used by all characters from the Auction House or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

The Guild Bank is a large shared storage space available to members of a Guild. It allows players to store and share items, materials, and gold within their community, making it easier to manage resources collectively.

You can access the Guild Bank at special NPCs located in major cities. Guild leaders have control over permissions, deciding which members can deposit or withdraw items and funds to maintain organization and security.

As the Guild grows, additional storage tabs can be purchased to expand the Guild Bank. This extra space helps support group activities like raiding, crafting, and other events, by providing plenty of room for important items.

The Pets Tab (Hotkey Shift + P) is the interface where you can view the details of your Tamed Pet, as well as your Mounts and Companions. 

For players using a Tamed Pet, the pets tab displays key information including the pet’s name, type, level, and stats.

In addition, the pet tab gives you full access to your mount and companion collections, allowing you to preview, summon, or dismiss your learned vanity or regular non-combat pets and Mounts from one convenient location.

These caches are reward chests earned by completing the Call Board Daily Quest. Designed as a catch-up mechanic, these caches are ideal for helping players quickly gear up for current content, especially if you're returning to the game or leveling a fresh character.

Each cache has a high chance to contain gear upgrades, from Dungeon gear to epic Raid loot from all previously released content, scaling up to the most recently released Raid. If you receive a cache from a daily quest requiring PvP activities, the gear from your cache will be Bloodforged.

These chests offer a reliable alternative to repetitive farming, giving you access to relevant power gains even if you're behind the current progression curve. They're especially helpful for preparing alts or off-specs for group content.

Worldforged Mystic Enchants are a special category of powerful enchants that can only be discovered through exploration, combat, and solving in-game challenges. Unlike regular mystic enchants, worldforged enchants cannot be traded, purchased, or reforged from regular Mystic Scrolls, they must be found in the world and unlocked through gameplay.

These enchants are hidden across the open world and are often obtained by defeating specific bosses, solving puzzles, interacting with secret objects, or exploring hidden areas.

To track your progress, open the Mystic Enchant menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab) and filter your collection by 'Not Collected -> Worldforged Enchants'. Hovering over any locked enchant in this list will give you a lore-friendly hint or clue guiding you to its location.
